query: A TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy has been reported in a single-phase BCC, dendritic state, with a yield strength of about 800 MPa and roughly 40% strain under lower-temperature testing, but at 1273 K it retains only 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain. For its use as an intermediate layer that transfers heat between W and CuCrZr while preserving structural integrity, what single intervention could overcome this loss of strength at elevated temperature? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the reported baseline, define the applicable thermal and mechanical boundary conditions, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled introduction of oxygen during processing — designed to in situ form a fine dispersion of TiO precipitates within the BCC matrix — will improve the high‐temperature yield strength of the TiVNbTa refractory HEA by retarding dislocation motion at 1273 K.
generation.material_initial_state: A single‐phase, dendritic BCC TiVNbTa alloy prepared by vacuum arc melting and annealed at ~1300 °C, with a yield strength of ~800 MPa at lower temperatures and a reduced yield strength of ~330 MPa at 1273 K.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled, minor oxygen addition (either during melting or via a post-melt annealing in a slightly oxygenated atmosphere) to promote the formation of uniformly dispersed, nano‐scale TiO precipitates within the BCC matrix.
generation.conditions: The alloy would be heat treated in an environment with a controlled oxygen partial pressure (e.g., an oxygen-doped inert atmosphere) at 1200–1300 °C for several hours to enable nucleation and growth of TiO particles, followed by rapid cooling. Mechanical testing should be conducted at 1273 K under tensile/compressive loading (target strains of ~30–40%) in an inert or vacuum environment to mimic the operating conditions when transferring heat between tungsten and CuCrZr.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of nanoscale, coherent or semi-coherent TiO precipitates that are uniformly distributed within the BCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: The TiO precipitates would serve as obstacles to dislocation motion (precipitation strengthening), especially under high-temperature conditions where thermal activation facilitates dislocation glide. This increased resistance to dislocation movement is expected to help retain higher yield strength at elevated temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline yield strength of ~330 MPa at 1273 K, the intervention is predicted to significantly improve high-temperature strength, potentially doubling or at least markedly increasing the yield strength, while maintaining acceptable ductility for the interlayer application.
generation.baseline: TiVNbTa alloy with ~800 MPa yield strength at lower temperatures but only ~330 MPa yield strength (and 30% compressive strain) at 1273 K.
generation.boundary: Applicable under high-temperature operation around 1273 K in environments (e.g., inert or vacuum conditions) that simulate the service conditions for an intermediate heat-transfer layer between tungsten (W) and CuCrZr; mechanical loading conditions representative of tensile/compressive stresses typical in such interfaces.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal oxygen content and heat-treatment schedule required to achieve a beneficial precipitate distribution must be tuned. There is also uncertainty regarding possible trade-offs, such as any adverse effects on ductility, thermal conductivity, or oxidation resistance beyond the designed precipitate formation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of the TiVNbTa alloy: one as a control processed under minimal oxygen conditions, and one with a deliberate, controlled oxygen addition followed by the tailored heat treatment to induce TiO precipitates. Use electron microscopy (SEM/TEM) to confirm precipitate formation and distribution. Then perform high-temperature mechanical tests at 1273 K under comparable tensile/compressive loading conditions.
measurements: Yield strength and compressive/tensile stress-strain curves at 1273 K
Precipitate size, density, and distribution via SEM/TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxygen-modified alloy does not show a statistically significant improvement in yield strength at 1273 K (e.g., less than a 10–20% increase over the 330 MPa baseline) or if the precipitate distribution is inconsistent or deleterious (severely reducing ductility or thermal conductivity), then the hypothesis that controlled oxygen addition via TiO precipitate formation enhances high-temperature strength is falsified.

Equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory HEA has been successfully synthesized by MA and SPS. It exhibits excellent mechanical properties with compressive yield strength of 2709 MPa, fracture strength of 3115 MPa and fracture strain of 11.4%. The sintered alloy consists of a BCC matrix phase, a minor BCC phase, and an FCC precipitated phase, identified as TiO. The average grain size of BCC matrix phase and TiO are measured to be 1.35 μm and 0.46 μm, respectively. Compared with the as-cast NbMoTaWVTi alloy, the compressive yield strength and fracture strength of the alloy in this work are extraordinarily elevated, while the ductility is slightly reduced. Thus, mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering is a promising way to further improve mechanical properties of the refractory HEA by means of grain refinement and precipitation strengthening.
